$comment: THE ROLLOUT CLOCK for check:ci-plan-implementation and for the Stop hook's
`plan-unimplemented` block. ONE set of numbers, read by BOTH halves, for the
reason plan-lifecycle.json's own $comment gives about `delete_days`:
duplicating a number into two scripts is how the two halves come to disagree
about the same tree on the same day. Neither half may inline these.
THE OPERATOR'S ASK, paraphrased because the verbatim wording carries a
first-person pronoun the house style keeps out of prose: the repo plans and
does not implement, and the stated aim is to eliminate 'planned but not
implemented'. Offered three narrower scopes (per-PR-diff, per-branch,
per-plan-adoption) after seeing the census, the operator chose ALL. So there
is no status exemption here: `draft` is this repo's DEFAULT header on plans
under active execution (wl_planfile.py's design note 4 measured that on
2026-09-02), and exempting it would exempt most of the debt and leave the
gate asserting almost nothing.
A DESCENDING CEILING, NOT A GRACE CLIFF, and the choice is argued rather
than inherited. agent-session-archival.json next door uses a cliff, and its
own $comment argues against that shape for exactly this case: a cliff is
silent until a date and then reds on the whole stock at once, 'blaming
whoever's branch runs CI next ... the exact shape that gets suppressed
within a day'. A ceiling instead reds only on a SHORTFALL, so every tick
buys slack immediately, the number is knowable a week in advance, and a
session that drains its share is never red at all.
ceiling(d) = max(floor_open, baseline_open - floor(d * drain_per_day))
where d = whole days from baseline_at to today, never negative.
THE EXIT IS ARITHMETIC, which is what keeps this from becoming the fourth
repeated-nag incident in this hook. Three are already on record --
PLAN-fix-stop-hook-completion-evidence-refire.md,
PLAN-stop-hook-refactor-enforcement.md and
PLAN-sweep-obligation-carry-forward.md -- and every one of them blocked with
no reachable exit. Here the block names the exact number of boxes that ends
it, and closing them ends it. That is why the block carries no fire cap: a
mission that goes quiet after two asks is not a mission, and a cap is only
needed when the exit is unreachable.
baseline_open WAS RE-MEASURED AGAINST THE LIVE TREE, not copied from the
design. PLAN-plan-implementation-enforcement.md Part 1.1 recorded 298 in-
scope open boxes on 2026-09-22 at ~21:10, and its own later text said 221. Both
are stale. An audit-and-tick sweep ran against this same checkout afterwards,
a peer session drained more boxes while this gate was being written, and this
gate's own implementation closed sixteen through the verb it adds. So the
number below is the one the gate's own census returns on the landing tree:
wl_checks.plan_records -> 120 plan files
minus wl_planfile.FINISHED_STATES, keeping only plans with >=1 open box
-> 19 plans, 189 open boxes (draft 112, ready 37, phase 15, mostly 8, partially 6, in-progress 5, mostly-done 4, closing 2)
The ledger .ci/config/plan-boxes.json agrees at 191 open / 619 done, which it
did not on 2026-09-22: the one Status:done plan that carried an open box
(PLAN-stop-hook-behavioral-hints.md:264) was ticked by that sweep, so the
hook's scope and the ledger's scope now coincide rather than differing by one.
They are still DIFFERENT QUESTIONS and the gate keeps applying the
FINISHED_STATES filter by import; the agreement is a fact about today's tree,
not a licence to drop the filter.
baseline_at IS THE LANDING DATE, not any plan's age. This is the operator's
own floated mechanism and it is adopted verbatim: nobody is punished for a
plan written before the rule existed, and the clock still starts immediately
and never stops. On day 0 the ceiling equals the live count, so both halves
are silent on the landing commit. The first thing this does in anger is on
day 1, at 184.
REVISED 2026-09-23, DAY 1, BEFORE THE FALSIFICATION TRIGGER FIRED: drain_per_day
moved from 7 to 11 and warn_slack from 20 to 35 on the operator's explicit
instruction, not because the two-week miss condition below was met -- it was
not; this is a deliberate, earlier policy change. The trigger observed:
authoring three real plan designs in one stretch (a normal, encouraged
activity, not debt) added 26 boxes in under an hour, a rate the original
10/day fallback was not sized against either. 11/day clears 191 boxes in 18
days rather than 28; widening warn_slack to 35 keeps the advisory-only band
proportionally wider so a session still gets roughly the same days of notice
before a red, given the steeper slope. The operator considered and declined
two structural alternatives offered at the same time: re-baselining
baseline_open/baseline_at to today's live count, and excluding Status:
proposed plans from the gate's scope entirely (a plan nobody has approved
for a build yet is arguably not "planned but not implemented" pressure).
Both remain on the table if 11/day still proves too steep.
HOW drain_per_day: 7 WAS ORIGINALLY CHOSEN, and what would have falsified
it. 7/day clears 191 boxes in 28 days. It is one working day's drainage of a
single 20-box plan every three days, a cadence this branch had demonstrably
sustained (14 plans and 188 boxes were authored on it in 16 days, and a
single sweep closed 77 in one evening). If the ceiling had been missed for
two consecutive weeks WHILE real work was landing, the number would have
been wrong; that trigger did not fire before this revision, which changed
the number for the different reason recorded above.
warn_slack: 35 (originally 20) is the humane band, the same device
plan-lifecycle.json's warn_days: 26 provides against delete_days: 33. Within
35 boxes of the ceiling the Stop hook speaks as an ADVISORY at priority 2;
over it, as a T_MISSION block; CI reds only when OVER. The band exists
because this gate is clock-driven -- its verdict can flip overnight with no
commit, which scripts/lib/suppression-liveness.ts normally bans -- so a
session learns the date it will go red several days before it does.
floor_open: 0 exists so that a future operator decision to hold a standing
floor is a config edit rather than a redesign. It is NOT used at landing, and
it is not an allowlist: it applies to the whole corpus or to nothing.
THE CLOCK DOES NOT STOP. There is no renewal, no extension verb, no
per-plan exemption and no allowlist anywhere in this gate.
docs/agent-reference/suppressions.md governs every escape hatch in this repo
and this one deliberately ships with none, because an allowlist here would be
an allowlist against 'implement the plan', which is the whole ask.
